chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: The obligatory salat (prayer) has become due while I am inside the Ka'bah; should I perform salat (prayer) in it? He said: Perform salat (prayer).

So this report does not conflict with the first two reports, because the proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon the state of necessity in which a person is unable to leave it. At that point, salat (prayer) in it is permissible for him, though that is disliked and not prohibited. This was made explicit in his saying, “The obligatory salat (prayer) is not proper inside the interior of the Ka'bah,” and that is explicit in indicating dislike. The first report, even if its wording is the wording of prohibition, its meaning is dislike, as indicated by what he explained in the second report and what has come concerning its permissibility in the third report.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity preventing normal action
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Ka'bah, the Sacred House in Makkah
key_terms.لَا تَصْلُحُ: is not proper or fitting, here indicating disapproval rather than prohibition
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: disliked in legal ruling, though not forbidden

ai.seo_question: Can obligatory salat (prayer) be performed inside the Ka'bah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if the obligatory salat (prayer) becomes due while a person is inside the Ka'bah, he may perform it there. The accompanying legal discussion explains that this permission is understood in a case of necessity, and that performing obligatory salat (prayer) inside the Ka'bah is regarded as makruh (disliked), not haram (forbidden).
